reports.title: CASELLA WASTE SYSTEMS, INC. ANNOUNCES THIRD QUARTER 2026 RESULTS

guidance.heading: Fiscal Year 2026 Outlook
section: The Company updated guidance for the fiscal year ending December 31, 2026 (“fiscal year 2026”) for the following ranges:
•Revenues between $2.100 billion and $2.110 billion (raised from a range of $2.090 billion to $2.110 billion);
•Adjusted EBITDA between $475 million and $481 million (narrowed from between $473 million and $483 million); and
•Net loss between $(10) and $(4) million (lowered from a range of net income between $0 million and $6 million).
The Company reaffirmed guidance for fiscal year 2026 by estimating results in the following ranges:
•Net cash provided by operating activities between $370 million and $380 million; and
•Adjusted Free Cash Flow between $200 million and $210 million.

desk.headline: Revenue up 15% to $559.2m, slightly below estimates; adjusted EPS $0.35 missed; EBITDA outlook narrowed, revenue range lifted
results: Revenue rose 15.2% to $559.2m, driven by acquisitions, solid waste price increases of 5.5% and higher landfill volumes; it came in just under the $562.9m analysts expected.
Adjusted EBITDA grew 11.4% to $133.5m, but the margin slipped to 23.9% from 24.7% as fuel costs, the Mid-Atlantic region and acquisitions weighed.
A $13.6m write-off of the abandoned Granite State landfill project pushed the company to a GAAP net loss of $7.0m (-$0.11 a share); adjusted EPS fell to $0.35 from $0.43, below the $0.38 estimate.
Six businesses with over $170m of yearly revenue have been bought so far in 2026; year-to-date adjusted free cash flow fell 7% to $111.1m.
Cash fell to $11.7m and debt rose to about $1.38bn as acquisitions were funded with borrowings.

guidance.summary: Casella tightened its 2026 adjusted EBITDA range around the same midpoint and lifted the bottom of its revenue range because of higher fuel fees. Cash flow targets were reaffirmed, while the GAAP outlook moved to a net loss after the landfill write-off.

points: The CEO admitted the Mid-Atlantic region fell short in Q3, but said new leadership, fuel surcharges and price rises lifted October margins over 3 points from a year ago.
An early look at 2027 points to about 7% revenue growth before new deals (around 5% organic) and 50–100 basis points of margin gain.
Management committed to at least 3 points of EBITDA margin expansion by the end of 2029, through fee discipline, productivity, back-office cuts and a review of weaker units.
Layoffs and new credit-card fees should each save about $5m a year, with benefits starting in Q4.
Deals will continue at roughly $150m of acquired revenue a year, with more weight on margins and faster integration.
call.source: Call transcript: The Motley Fool, 10 Nov 2026

watch: Whether the Mid-Atlantic margin recovery seen in October holds through Q4 and into 2027.
Delivery of the promised G&A savings and the first steps of the 2029 margin plan.
Debt levels as acquisitions continue, and the formal 2027 guidance.
